title: Alternatives to Partial Demolition of Ellison Building
what_it_is: Alternatives to Partial Demolition of Ellison Building

sections.label: Ellison Building demolition questions
sections.summary: An MP asks the Minister for National Development about demolition and rebuilding of three Ellison Building units and related studies, consultations and heritage loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in respect of the demolition and rebuilding of three units of Ellison Building (a) whether LTA and URA have considered realigning the North-South Expressway without affecting Ellison Building when the alignment plan was announced in 2011; (b) whether studies were made before arriving at this option and, if so, whether they were disclosed; (c) whether LTA and URA have consulted with stakeholders, such as the long-term tenants of the building, residents living in the area and heritage organisations and, if not, what are the reasons; (d) what is the loss in heritage value created by this option; (e) what are the mitigation measures considered before deciding on this option; and (f) why is this decision the best option.

sections.label: NSC studies avoid Rex Cinema
sections.summary: Agencies studied and developed a solution for the NSC to avoid Rex Cinema completely, reducing impact on Ellison Building to one corner shophouse unit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Indeed, the agencies had worked hard to carry out extensive studies and eventually managed to develop a solution for the NSC to avoid Rex Cinema completely.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: And I am sure the Member has seen maps that show this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: These engineering studies were concluded only recently, and the result is that the impact on Ellison Building can, under current plans, be reduced to one corner shophouse unit, instead of a larger portion or the entire building.

sections.label: Implementation plans after discussions
sections.summary: The Government will finalise its implementation plans after these discussions are concluded.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Government will finalise its implementation plans after these discussions are concluded.

sections.label: Mandatory culture impact assessment
sections.summary: A check is raised on whether the Ministry would consider making culture impact assessment mandatory and compulsory in such development projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The third thing that I want to check is: would the Ministry consider making culture impact assessment mandatory and compulsory in such development projects?

sections.label: Studying cultural impact assessment
sections.summary: The Member asked about cultural impact assessment covering environment, community and heritage, which needs careful study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Member asked about cultural impact assessment embodying various strands of impact on the environment, community, heritage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is something we need to study carefully.

sections.label: Impacts on businesses and amenities
sections.summary: These matters impact businesses, homes, public amenities, parks and greenery, and work is needed before engaging the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They are important but they also impact people's businesses, homes, public amenities, parks and greenery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We need to do work from conception to a certain level of certainty before we then engage the community.
